items.stem: The strongest argument for continuous feedback over a single annual review is that it:

options.text: Reduces the manager's workload to zero
options.rationale: Continuous feedback is ongoing work, not an elimination of effort.

options.text: Lets people adjust while there is still time to improve
options.rationale: Correct: timely feedback allows course-correction rather than a year-end surprise.

options.text: Removes the need for any documentation
options.rationale: Documentation still matters for fairness and decisions.

options.text: Guarantees everyone gets a top rating
options.rationale: Feedback frequency does not inflate ratings.

items.explanation: Correct: timely feedback allows course-correction rather than a year-end surprise.

items.stem: Before moving to formal discipline, a manager facing underperformance should first:

options.text: Assume the person is not trying and issue a warning
options.rationale: Assuming lack of effort skips diagnosis and risks unfairness.

options.text: Diagnose whether the cause is skill, clarity, resources or motivation
options.rationale: Correct: identifying the real cause lets the manager choose the right response.

options.text: Reassign the work to someone else immediately
options.rationale: Reassignment avoids rather than addresses the performance issue.

options.text: Lower the person's goals without discussion
options.rationale: Silently lowering goals neither diagnoses nor resolves the problem.

items.explanation: Correct: identifying the real cause lets the manager choose the right response.

items.stem: In the 70-20-10 model of development, which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

options.text: Most development comes from challenging on-the-job experience
options.rationale: Correct: the '70' reflects learning through real work and stretch tasks.

options.text: Learning from others, such as coaching, is a meaningful share
options.rationale: Correct: the '20' covers learning from relationships and feedback.

options.text: Formal courses should make up the large majority of development
options.rationale: Formal training is the smallest share (the '10'), not the majority.

options.text: On-the-job experience plays almost no role
options.rationale: Experience is the largest driver, not a minor one.

items.explanation: Correct: the '70' reflects learning through real work and stretch tasks.; Correct: the '20' covers learning from relationships and feedback.
